newsitem.title: USA: Clinton shies away from capital gains tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Clinton shies away from capital gains tax cut.

text.p: President Clinton has shied away from proposing a targeted capital gains tax cut, despite initial interest in such a plan, officials said on Monday.
"There was a lot of interest on the part of the president," said one administration official, who declined to be named. "But that now seems to have sunk from view."

Officials said Clinton's enthusiasm for a targeted capital gains tax cut, perhaps aimed at new investment by small businesses, waned after his Republican rival Bob Dole proposed a broad-based tax reduction on investment.

Dole, who trails Clinton in the opinion polls with about 2-1/2 months to go until the November 5 election, has called for a halving of the maximum capital gains tax rate, to 14 percent. "Suddenly, when Dole came out with his proposal, it
just would have looked too much like pandering, too much like me-tooism, if we had come out with our own plan," the administration official said.
